result: The authors tested 10 putative essential genes identified by In-seq and confirmed that three genes (A1S_0137, A1S_2249, and A1S_3387/Aeg1) are essential for A. baumannii viability on rich medium, with Aeg1 also essential on minimal medium. This led to the conclusion that essentiality assignments from In-seq require individual verification.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the confirmation of Aeg1 as an essential gene and do not challenge the validation approach or the conclusion that only 3 of 10 tested genes were confirmed essential. The editor states 'the authors confirm that one of the genes classified as essential in a Tn-mutagenesis study in A. baumannii, Aeg1, is, in fact, an essential gene.'

result: Depletion of Aeg1 causes cell elongation/filamentation in A. baumannii, with >96% of cells becoming elongated (5-10+ μm) after 18 hr without arabinose, and this phenotype can be partially reversed by re-addition of arabinose.
evaluation: Both reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding as a strength. The editor states 'the strength of the work is the discovery that the depletion of Aeg1 leads to cell filamentation' and the anonymous reviewer similarly notes 'the strength of the work is that it discovered that the depletion of Aeg1 leads to cell filamentation.'

result: Suppressor mutants M1 and M2 that can grow without Aeg1 both carry an E202K mutation in FtsA. Expression of FtsAE202K, but not wild-type FtsA, suppresses the growth defect and restores normal cell morphology in Aeg1-depleted strains.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this as a key finding. The editor notes 'gain-of-function mutations in cell division genes FtsB and FtsL rescue the lethality of Aeg1 depletion' and the anonymous reviewer states 'activation mutations in various cell division genes can suppress the requirement for Aeg1.' The FtsAE202K suppression is not specifically challenged.

result: FtsA variants D124A and V144L partially rescue growth of Aeg1-depleted strains, while FtsAQ285W cannot detectably suppress Aeg1 depletion.
evaluation: The reviewer explicitly challenges this claim, stating 'the spotting rescue assay showed that only FtsB-E56A and FtsA-E202K was able to bypass Aeg1 depletion (full dilution set comparable to that of Aeg1 complementation), but the main text claimed that FtsA-D124A and V144L...also rescued the growth. These claims could be misleading.'

result: Aeg1 localizes to the septum of dividing cells as shown by fluorescence microscopy.
evaluation: Reviewers raise significant concerns about localization data quality and functionality of fusion proteins. The editor states 'Aeg1's localization pattern...require further characterization of the functionality of fluorescent fusion proteins, fluorescence images of higher quality.' The reviewer notes 'fluorescent images of these fusion proteins were diffusive, and only a few cells showed the expected midcell/membrane localization pattern' and suggests fusion proteins may be cleaved, requiring Western blot validation.

result: Aeg1 interacts with multiple divisome proteins (ZipA, FtsK, FtsL, FtsB, FtsN) in bacterial two-hybrid assays, with ZipA and FtsN showing higher binding affinity regardless of T25 fusion orientation.
evaluation: The reviewer challenges the strength of these interactions, stating 'In the two-hybrid assay, only ZipA and FtsN showed significant interactions with Aeg1, as judged by the darkness of the blue spots. FtsL and FtsB showed pale spots. The quantified values accompanying this figure did not appear to agree with the image.' Additionally, concerns about membrane topology of ZipA in the assay are raised.

result: Aeg1 colocalizes with ZipA, FtsL, FtsB, and FtsN at the division site.
evaluation: Reviewers express serious concerns about colocalization data. The reviewer states 'Colocalization images did not show significant midcell localizations for each fluorescent protein; most cells showed diffusive cytoplasmic fluorescence' and notes 'In all other species, midcell localization of cell division proteins is prominent in dividing cells, especially for early division proteins such as ZipA (at least 40-50% of cells show midcell bands).' Concerns about protein aggregates versus functional localization are raised.

result: In Aeg1-depleted cells, core division proteins (ZipA, FtsB, FtsL, FtsN) display midcell mistargeting, suggesting Aeg1 plays a role in positioning these proteins at the septum.
evaluation: The editor states 'it is unclear whether proteins are at the division site under the wildtype condition and when Aeg1 is depleted, and whether Aeg1 is indeed required for a set of division proteins to the division site.' The reviewer notes the paradox that 'in Aeg1 depletion strains, some cells...showed roughly regularly spaced puncta in long filamentous cells. It is hard to explain why this was observed if, under the WT condition, these fusions do not localize to the midcell.'

result: Constitutively active mutants of FtsB (FtsBE65A) and FtsL (FtsLQ70K) can bypass the requirement for Aeg1, with FtsBE65A showing complete rescue and FtsLQ70K showing partial rescue, while FtsBD68H cannot suppress.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge suppression by gain-of-function mutants as a strength, the anonymous reviewer specifically challenges the extent of rescue, stating 'the spotting rescue assay showed that only FtsB-E56A and FtsA-E202K was able to bypass Aeg1 depletion (full dilution set comparable to that of Aeg1 complementation),' suggesting FtsL rescue may be overstated.

result: Overexpression of FtsW activation mutants (FtsWM254I and FtsWS274G) detectably rescues growth of Aeg1-depleted strains.
evaluation: The reviewer explicitly challenges this claim, stating 'the spotting rescue assay showed that only FtsB-E56A and FtsA-E202K was able to bypass Aeg1 depletion (full dilution set comparable to that of Aeg1 complementation), but the main text claimed that...FtsW-M254I and S274G also rescued the growth. These claims could be misleading.'

result: The authors propose a model in which Aeg1 functions as an early-arriving divisome component that collaborates with FtsN to activate FtsQLB and FtsA, which subsequently activate FtsWI for septal peptidoglycan synthesis. This model is based on suppression by constitutively active mutants and protein interaction data.
evaluation: The editor concludes 'the critical role of Aeg1 in the assembly of the A. baumannii divisome has yet to be established unambiguously' and 'the work's weakness is that it lacks convincing evidence to define Aeg1's place or role in the divisome assembly pathway.' While suppression data support an upstream role, the localization and interaction data underlying the specific mechanistic model are questioned.

result: Aeg1 has orthologs in many Gram-negative bacteria including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Salmonella enterica, Moraxellaceae, and some E. coli strains (80-100% identity), but appears absent in E. coli K12.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the sequence analysis or distribution of Aeg1 orthologs. This bioinformatic finding is presented as context and is not disputed.

result: The N-terminal domain of Aeg1 is essential for its activity, as an N-terminal deletion mutant cannot restore growth.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this finding. The result from C-terminal fusion constructs that still show activity (C31) actually supports the interpretation that the N-terminus is functionally important, which the reviewer acknowledges positively.
